judgments.lesson: There is no weekend risk premium in carry crosses net of costs, and no weekday-overnight premium either. On AUDJPY every one of the 16 pre-registered arms lost in design (2010-2017, 412 trades per arm): the eight Friday-to-Monday arms made -0.008 to -0.030 R (t -1.2 to -2.5) and the eight Monday-to-Tuesday overnight controls -0.004 to -0.026 R (t -0.3 to -4.3); the check period was flat (-0.021 to +0.006 R). Holding AUDJPY across the Friday-to-Monday gap costs the weekend-edge spread (3-4 pips round trip including commission) and earns nothing in price; the premium that equities show overnight does not exist in FX carry pairs at this horizon. Stage B never ran, so NZDJPY, AUDUSD, NZDUSD and EURJPY are unmeasured, but the primary market was the best-motivated one and the control arms lost too. Do not retry with other entry or exit hours, the Thursday-to-Monday hold, the short side (a snooped flip), EURJPY or GBPJPY stage A, a VIX or realised-vol gate, or an equity-state aux condition.
judgments.notes: Killed at GA_stage_a_floor on AUDJPY. The design worked as intended: the control arm was in the grid, the exit and cost rules were fixed before the run after the Critic's revisions, and the negative is unambiguous. This was the first adequately powered test in three cycles (412 design trades per arm) and it closes the weekend-hold horizon for FX in this programme.

hypotheses.title: Liquidity-withdrawal reversal: fade a large one-hour move only when the quoted spread blew out during it (dealers withdrew), with no-spread-condition and scheduled-news control arms, on USDJPY first
hypotheses.rationale: Mechanism (Nagel 2012, 'Evaporating liquidity'; Brunnermeier and Pedersen 2009; Mancini, Ranaldo and Wrampelmeyer 2013 for FX): short-term price reversals are the compensation liquidity providers earn for absorbing order imbalances, and that compensation is large only when liquidity supply is scarce. In FX the scarcity is observable: when dealers and ECN liquidity providers pull or widen their quotes, the top-of-book spread widens several-fold against its normal level at that time of day. A large move that happens while quotes are withdrawn is, in part, a price concession paid by an impatient liquidity demander (a stop cascade, a forced hedger, a margin-driven seller) to the few providers still quoting; once quoting resumes, the concession is competed away and the price retraces. The same-sized move made with normal, tight quotes is information being priced by a deep book and should not retrace; this is what every prior fade in this programme measured, and they all lost (session reversal, Asian-extreme fade, quiet-hours Bollinger fade, sweep fades, one-day shock fade -0.10 R on EURUSD). Those tests conditioned on clock, level or size, never on the state of liquidity supply, so their negatives are consistent with this hypothesis rather than against it; the tick-volume test (fx_volume_climax_reversal) tried to measure liquidity demand with a quantity that does not measure it, and its lesson forbids volume, not spread. The quoted spread is the one data dimension in this store that no prior test has used as a signal input. Design: bars M15 on USDJPY (0.6 pip median spread, the classic liquidity-gap currency; the 2010-05-06, 2011-03-17, 2013-05-23, 2015-08-24 and 2016-06-24 episodes are in the design years). The state is the bar's quoted-spread proxy relative to the median of the same 15-minute slot over its previous 20 occurrences, so the daily spread profile and the rollover widening cancel out; the trigger is a one-hour mid-price move of at least 0.25 or 0.40 x ATR20. Two controls sit in the grid: spread_ratio_min = 1 (no spread condition; the plain intraday shock fade, which the mechanism predicts to be about zero or negative) and exclude_news = false (keeps moves inside the three scheduled-announcement blocks, 12:00-15:30, 18:00-20:00 and 03:00-05:00 UTC, plus the 20:45-22:15 rollover; these are information-driven and the mechanism predicts no reversal there, which the NFP fade result of -0.12 R already suggests). The hypothesis arm is spread_ratio_min >= 2 with exclude_news = true. Market-fact counts from the design years (counts only, no outcomes): USDJPY M15 bars with spread ratio >= 2 and a one-hour move >= 0.25 x ATR20 number about 920, of which about 55 percent sit inside the news blocks; outside the blocks there are roughly 370 bars forming about 230 distinct episodes (29 per year), and about 230 episodes on EURUSD; the ratio >= 3 arm has only about 65 non-news episodes and is a surface point, not the primary. Costs are the real threat and are accepted up front: the fill right after a liquidity event pays whatever spread is quoted at the next open, so a 17-pip move (0.25 x ATR20) faded at a 1.5-2 pip spread plus 0.2 pip slippage plus about 0.8 pip commission costs 0.13-0.18 R, and the entry_delay_bars = 1 arm (order placed one bar later, after quotes normally refill) measures how much of the retracement survives waiting 15 minutes for a cheaper fill. Every arm must report the mean entry spread so the cost question is answered in the open. Expected: the hypothesis arm retraces 25-40 percent of the move within two hours on average (+0.25 to +0.40 R gross), net +0.08 R after costs with sd about 0.6 R, so with 230 trades design t is about 1.5-2.5; the control arm should be at or below zero. Human execution: a prop trader with a spread alert on the platform can take this (one order, a stop at the move size, a two-hour time exit); it is not a scalp.
hypotheses.rules:
All times UTC. Bars: M15, labelled by open time; a bar's close time is ts + 15 minutes. Bars are sparse; locate by timestamp and never assume one bar per slot.

DEFINITIONS (all computed from closed bars 0..i):
- mid_c[i] = (bid_c[i] + ask_c[i]) / 2. The one-hour move ending at bar i is move[i] = mid_c[i] - mid_c[i-4]; require i >= 4 and ts[i] - ts[i-4] <= 75 minutes, otherwise no signal at i.
- ATR20[i] = F.atr_prev(F.daily_bars(m), 20) mapped to bars (known at the start of the trading day); require finite and > 0.
- Quoted-spread proxy of bar i: spr[i] = max(ask_o[i] - bid_o[i], ask_c[i] - bid_c[i], ask_h[i] - bid_h[i], ask_l[i] - bid_l[i]) (price units).
- Slot of bar i: slot[i] = F.minute_of_day_utc(m)[i] (0..1425 in steps of 15). norm[i] = median of spr over the previous 20 bars that share slot[i], strictly before bar i (not including i); require 20 such bars exist and norm[i] > 0, otherwise no signal at i. ratio[i] = spr[i] / norm[i].
- News blocks (UTC, half-open): [03:00, 05:00), [12:00, 15:30), [18:00, 20:00), [20:45, 22:15). The move window of bar i is [ts[i] + 15 min - 60 min, ts[i] + 15 min). When exclude_news is true, no signal at i if the move window overlaps any block (compare minute-of-day of the window start and end against each block; all blocks lie inside one UTC day).

SIGNAL CONDITION at bar i: |move[i]| >= move_atr_min * ATR20[i] AND ratio[i] >= spread_ratio_min AND (exclude_news is false OR the move window is outside all blocks). spread_ratio_min = 1 is the no-spread-condition control arm (ratio >= 1 is always true wherever norm is defined).

ONE TRADE PER EPISODE: scan candidate bars in ascending order; accept bar i only if i >= last_accepted + cooldown_bars (cooldown_bars = 12, i.e. three hours), where last_accepted is the last accepted signal bar; set last_accepted = i on acceptance.

ORDER PLACEMENT: let j = i + entry_delay_bars (entry_delay_bars 0 or 1); require j < m.n and, when entry_delay_bars = 1, ts[j] - ts[i] <= 30 minutes (otherwise skip the episode). All signal fields are written at index j and use only information from bars <= j (the condition was decided at i <= j).
- If move[i] > 0: entry_short[j] = True (fade an up move). If move[i] < 0: entry_long[j] = True (fade a down move).
- entry_type[j] = 0 (market at the open of bar j + 1, ask for longs, bid for shorts), valid_bars[j] = 1.
- sl_dist[j] = stop_mult * |move[i]| with stop_mult = 1.0 (so 1 R = the size of the move being faded); always > 0 because |move[i]| >= move_atr_min * ATR20 > 0.
- tp_dist[j] = NaN (no target; the time exit measures the mean retracement).
- max_bars[j] = hold_bars = 8 (close at the open of the bar after holding eight M15 bars, about two hours).
- No exit_long / exit_short signals; no other filters; no pyramiding (the executor blocks entries while a position is open).

PARAMETERS: spread_ratio_min (grid 1, 2, 3), move_atr_min (grid 0.25, 0.40), exclude_news (grid true, false), entry_delay_bars (grid 0, 1); fixed: stop_mult 1.0, hold_bars 8, cooldown_bars 12, norm_window 20, max_gap_min 75. Every one of these is read from p.

REPORTING (stage A table and stage C): for every arm report the number of episodes, avg R, t, the mean quoted spread at the fill bar's open in pips, and gross R before spread and commission; report design years individually.

pre_registered.kill_if: (1) Stage A floor on USDJPY applies to the hypothesis arms only: if the best combination in design is a control arm (spread_ratio_min = 1 or exclude_news = false) the hypothesis is dead regardless of its numbers, because then the reversal, if any, is not a liquidity effect; among the hypothesis arms (spread_ratio_min >= 2 and exclude_news = true) the best must have design avg R > 0 and t >= 1 with at least 150 episodes. (2) Control: at the chosen move_atr_min and entry_delay_bars, avg R(spread_ratio_min = 2, exclude_news = true) minus avg R(spread_ratio_min = 1, exclude_news = true) must be >= +0.08 R in design; if the plain intraday shock fade earns as much, the spread adds nothing and the hypothesis dies. (3) Information control: at the chosen arm, the news version (exclude_news = false) must not beat the non-news version by more than 0.05 R in design; if moves inside the scheduled-announcement blocks revert more, the effect is overreaction to news, not liquidity provision, and the liquidity label is scrapped with that lesson. (4) Costs: the hard gate (positive at 1.5x costs) stands; the mean fill spread per arm is reported, and if the entry_delay_bars = 0 arm is positive gross but negative net while the delay = 1 arm is also negative, the lesson is that the concession is real but belongs to the liquidity providers who are already quoting, not to a market-order taker. (5) Regime: at least half of the design years positive at the chosen arm. (6) Stage B: the chosen arm must be positive in design on at least 3 of the 8 markets, and the pooled check must be positive with at least 30 trades (hard gate). Honest expectation: about 230 non-news episodes on USDJPY in design, net +0.08 R, design t 1.5-2.5; the ratio >= 3 arm (about 65 episodes) is underpowered and is a surface point, not a primary; the most likely failure is cost, because the fade is entered at a spread that is still wide.

hypotheses.why_different: Every prior fade in the index conditioned on the clock (session reversal, Tokyo-open contrarian, quiet-hours Bollinger fade, night scalp), on a price level (sweeps of the previous session's extreme, round numbers, Asian-range fade), on the size of a one-day move (shock fade, z-score fade) or on tick volume (volume climax); none conditioned on the state of liquidity supply, and none measured the quoted spread at all. This hypothesis uses the spread as the state variable, works at the intraday episode horizon (one-hour moves on M15 bars) rather than the session or day, and carries its own falsification structure: a no-spread-condition arm that reproduces the known negative baseline inside the same design, and a scheduled-news arm that the mechanism predicts to be worse. The tick-volume lesson forbids volume as an input and the follow-the-shock mirror; neither is used here. The NFP fade (edge_hunt) faded a single scheduled release at a fixed clock time, which is exactly the information-driven case this design puts in the control arm.

direction_note: Cycle 6 scraps the weekend-premium test with a lesson (no weekend or weekday-overnight premium in AUDJPY net of costs; all 16 arms negative in design, check flat) and registers one hypothesis, chosen because it is the last unused dimension of this data store: the quoted spread as a measure of liquidity supply. Before choosing it I checked the remaining candidates against the reports: the full close-to-open index overnight premium was already measured (index_anomalies E2a/E2b on Nasdaq, design -0.03 to -0.05 R, check negative) and the European-open version died on costs; the atlas scanned every clock window on all weekdays plus Wednesday/Thursday, gotobi, holiday-adjacent and k-th-weekday day types, so no new calendar idea can clear its t >= 3.7 bar; cross-sectional 'idiosyncratic' cross moves do not exist in FX because triangular consistency makes every pair return an exact difference of currency factors; XAGUSD, GER40, UK100, US30 are not in the data store, USA500 ends 2025-05, and JP225 has no Tokyo-morning bars in 2015-2017. The liquidity-state test has about 230 non-news episodes on USDJPY in design, carries its own controls (no-spread-condition arm, scheduled-news arm, one-bar entry delay for the cost question) and will most likely fail on the fill spread; if it fails, the liquidity-provision family is closed for good and the honest statement to the user stands: with price, spread and clock data alone the hypothesis space reachable here is exhausted after six cycles and the gj-strat scans before them. The next useful inputs are external: a scheduled-event calendar with surprise sizes, retail positioning (the broker long/short ratios), options risk reversals and implied vol, and the FX swap basis; without them the remaining lever for the Alpha Swing pass probability is the sizing and risk design of the USDJPY basket, which is a simulation task, not a hypothesis. Engine notes for later cycles: the M15 feed has about 195,000 design bars per major; the same-slot spread median needs 20 prior occurrences, so the first month of 2010 is unusable; the Builder must use mid prices for the move so a spread blow-out alone cannot register as a bid-side move.
